# 2 The Method's Character and Affinities

Pragmatism represents a perfectly familiar attitude in philosophy, the empiricist attitude, but it represents it,[^1] both in a more radical and in a less objectionable form than it has ever yet assumed.[^2] A pragmatist turns his back resolutely and once for all upon a lot of inveterate habits dear to professional philosophers.[^3] He turns away from abstraction and insufficiency, from verbal solutions, from bad a priori reasons, from fixed principles, closed systems, and pretended absolutes and origins.[^4] He turns towards concreteness and adequacy, towards facts, towards action, and towards power.[^5] That means the empiricist temper regnant, and the rationalist temper sincerely given up.[^6] It means the open air and possibilities of nature, as against dogma, artificiality and the pretence of finality in truth.[^7]

At the same time it does not stand for any special results.[^8] It is a method only.[^9] But the general triumph of that method would mean an enormous change in[^10] the 'temperament' of philosophy.[^11] Teachers of the ultra-rationalistic type would be frozen out.[^12] Science and metaphysics would come much nearer together, would in fact work absolutely hand in hand.[^13]

Metaphysics has usually followed a very primitive kind of quest.[^14] The universe has always appeared to the natural mind as a kind of enigma, of which the key must be sought in the shape of some illuminating or power-bringing word or name.[^15] That word names the universe's PRINCIPLE, and to possess it is, after a fashion, to possess the universe itself.[^16] 'God,' 'Matter,' 'Reason,' 'the Absolute,' 'Energy,' are so many solving names.[^17] You can rest when you have them.[^18] You are at the end of your metaphysical quest.[^19]

But if you follow the pragmatic method, you cannot look on any such word as closing your quest.[^20] You must bring out of each word its practical cash-value, set it at work within the stream of your experience.[^21] It appears less as a solution, then, than as a program for more work, and more particularly as an indication of the ways in which existing realities may be CHANGED.[^22]

THEORIES THUS BECOME INSTRUMENTS, NOT ANSWERS TO ENIGMAS, IN WHICH WE CAN REST.[^23] We don't lie back upon them, we move forward, and, on occasion, make nature over again by their aid.[^24] Pragmatism unstiffens all our theories, limbers them up and sets each one at work.[^25] Being nothing essentially new, it harmonizes with many ancient philosophic tendencies.[^26] It agrees with nominalism for instance, in always appealing to particulars; with utilitarianism in emphasizing practical aspects; with positivism in its disdain for verbal solutions, useless questions, and metaphysical abstractions.[^27]

All these, you see, are ANTI-INTELLECTUALIST tendencies.[^28] Against rationalism as a pretension and a method, pragmatism is fully armed and militant.[^29] But, at the outset, at least, it stands for no particular results.[^30] It has no dogmas, and no doctrines save its method.[^31] As the young Italian pragmatist Papini has well said, it lies in the midst of our theories, like a corridor in a hotel.[^32] Innumerable chambers open out of it.[^33] In one you may find a man writing an atheistic volume; in the next someone on his knees praying for faith and strength; in a third a chemist investigating a body's properties.[^34] In a fourth a system of idealistic metaphysics is being excogitated; in a fifth the impossibility of metaphysics is being shown.[^35] But they all own the corridor, and all must pass through it if they want a practicable way of getting into or out of their respective rooms.[^36]

No particular results then, so far, but only an attitude of orientation, is what the pragmatic method means.[^37] THE ATTITUDE OF LOOKING AWAY FROM FIRST THINGS, PRINCIPLES, 'CATEGORIES,' SUPPOSED NECESSITIES; AND OF LOOKING TOWARDS LAST THINGS, FRUITS, CONSEQUENCES, FACTS.[^38]

Meanwhile the word pragmatism has come to be used in a still wider sense, as meaning also a certain theory of TRUTH.[^39]
